newsitem.title: ITALY: Europeans from Sierra Leone arrive in Italy.
newsitem.headline: Europeans from Sierra Leone arrive in Italy.

text.p: A group of European citizens evacuated from violence after a coup in Sierra Leone flew to Rome on Sunday on an Italian airforce Boeing 707, airport officials said.
They said the flight from Conakry in neighbouring Guinea carried 72 Italians, a Romanian, a Belgian, three Sierra Leonians, six Britons and six Germans.
"Some of the rebels shot at the door of my room to try and get in," Briton Joe Dogherty from Bath told Italian reporters on arriving at Rome's main Fiumicino airport. "Others had their houses looted.
"We had problems getting food, all the shops were closed or burned. There were armed men in the streets and we all sought refuge where we could."
Officials said the Britons would be returning home later on Sunday on scheduled flights to Manchester and London.
U.S. marines were evacuating remaining Westerners in Sierra Leone on Sunday. Widespread looting and violence has erupted after the coup a week ago.
The United Nations, the Organisation of African Unity and the West African alliance ECOWAS have condemned the coup, led by Major Johnny Paul Koromah.
They have called on the military to step aside and restore power to elected President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah.
